constraints: The RTL module key_loader_ctrl is fewer than 150 lines of synthesizable Verilog-2001.
The module exposes exactly the ports listed in the interface section; no additional ports.
The RTL is provided as-is and must not be modified by the participant; all analysis is reported in the separate answer file.
The design_brief.md describes intended functional behavior (key loading over the bus, and zeroize-on-demand) without describing any known defect.

functional_requirements.requirement: trojan_report.json must be valid JSON containing top-level fields: 'candidates' (a non-empty array), 'summary' (string), and 'tool_version_or_method' (string describing how the analysis was performed, e.g. manual review, formal tool, simulation).

Each entry in 'candidates' must contain the fields: 'signal_or_net' (string), 'location_hint' (string identifying the RTL construct, e.g. a label, always block, or line range), 'trigger_condition' (string describing the input/state condition that activates the anomaly), and 'confidence' (a number between 0.0 and 1.0).

At least one candidate entry must explicitly describe a condition involving simultaneous assertion of zeroize and bus_busy (or an equivalent bus-transaction-in-progress state) as the trigger for the key register failing to clear.

The report must state, for the highest-confidence candidate, what the expected correct behavior of key_q should have been under the identified trigger condition (i.e. that key_q should equal 32'b0), enabling a reader to verify the claim by inspection or simulation of inputs/key_loader_ctrl.v.

interface: Module under analysis: key_loader_ctrl, located in inputs/key_loader_ctrl.v. Port list (exact): module key_loader_ctrl(input wire clk, input wire rst_n, input wire [31:0] bus_data, input wire bus_wr, input wire zeroize, output wire bus_busy, output wire [31:0] key_q). Semantics: clk is the system clock; rst_n is active-low synchronous reset; bus_data is the 32-bit data bus carrying key material to be loaded (secret-bearing input); bus_wr, when asserted for one or more cycles, initiates a bus write transaction that drives bus_busy high for the duration of the transfer; zeroize is a control input that, per the design intent, must force key_q to 32'b0 on the next clock edge whenever asserted, irrespective of bus_busy; bus_busy is a status output indicating an in-progress bus transaction; key_q is the 32-bit registered key output (the value participants must show can be forced to leak old key material). The participant submission is NOT code -- it is an analysis answer file at submission/trojan_report.json, described in response_format.
objective: You are given the RTL source for a key-loading controller module (key_loader_ctrl) used in a cryptographic subsystem. The module manages loading of a 32-bit key register from a bus, and supports an emergency zeroize function that is supposed to clear the key register to all zeros whenever the zeroize input is asserted, regardless of other bus activity. Analyze the provided RTL to determine whether the implementation faithfully clears the key register under all conditions in which zeroize is asserted. Produce a structured analysis report identifying any logic construct(s) that could cause the key register to retain its previous value instead of being cleared when zeroize is asserted, including the exact signal/state conditions under which this occurs, the RTL line/label of the offending logic, and your confidence that this is an intentionally inserted defect versus a benign design artifact.
response_format: Submit a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json with the schema: {"candidates": [{"signal_or_net": string, "location_hint": string, "trigger_condition": string, "confidence": number}], "summary": string, "tool_version_or_method": string}. The file must be valid UTF-8 JSON parseable with a standard JSON parser; no comments or trailing commas.
